newsitem.title: USA: Nationwide Insurance to manage property exposures.
newsitem.headline: Nationwide Insurance to manage property exposures.

text.p: Nationwide Insurance said Monday it will use new deductibles on wind storm damage coverage to manage property exposures and to ease the cost pressure on home and commercial property insurance.

Early next year the company said it plans to exclude wind storm coverage from homeowners insurance policies in areas where wind storm coverage is available through the Florida Windstorm Underwriting Association.

Also in 1997, in the 19 counties in southern Florida where loss potential is high (roughly the bottom 35 percent of Florida south of a line running from Tampa to Vero Beach), the company said a $500 deductible on wind storm damages will be applied to homeowners policies with coverages under $100,000.

Plans call for applying a two percent wind storm deductible to homeowners polices with coverage amounts above $100,000. The company said deductibles would become effective when policies are renewed. Also planned are variable deductibles for wind storm damages, ranging from 2 percent to 5 percent, to be applied to all commercial policies in those counties.
No one at the company was available to elaborate.
